section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concrete Vector
section_1.content: Briefly revisit vectors as 'arrows' in 2D or 3D space. Establish the two fundamental operations: Addition (head-to-tail) and Scalar Multiplication (stretching/shrinking). This ensures the audience understands the 'behavior' we are about to generalize.
section_1.example: An arrow pointing (3, 2) on a graph represents a force or displacement. If we double the force, the arrow stretches; if we add another force, the arrows combine geometrically.

section_2.title: The Concept of Abstraction
section_2.content: Introduce the idea that 'Vector-ness' isn't about being an arrow; it's about following a set of rules. We define a Vector Space as a collection of objects (vectors) that can be added together and scaled by numbers, while staying within the same collection.
section_2.example: Think of a 'Color Mixing Robot'. If it mixes Blue and Red, it gets Purple (another color). If it uses half as much Red, it gets a lighter shade. As long as the results are still 'colors', we have the basis of a vector space.

section_3.title: The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game
section_3.content: Present the 8 formal axioms (Commutativity, Associativity, Distributive properties, Identity, and Zero vector) through a visual checklist. Explain that any set of objects passing these tests qualifies as an 'Abstract Vector Space'.
section_3.example: Visualizing a 'Zero Element': In a space of functions, the 'Zero Vector' is the flat line y=0. In a space of matrices, it's a grid of zeros. Adding 'Zero' to any object must leave it unchanged.

section_4.title: Exotic Examples: Functions as Vectors
section_4.content: Demonstrate that polynomials or continuous functions are vectors. If you add two curves, you get a new curve. if you scale a curve, it changes height. This is the 'aha!' moment where students see vectors as more than just coordinates.
section_4.example: Imagine a 'Sound Synthesizer'. Each sound wave is a vector. Adding two waves creates a chord (superposition). Scaling a wave changes its volume. Therefore, the set of all possible sounds is an abstract vector space.

section_5.title: Why it Matters: The Power of Generalization
section_5.content: Conclude by explaining that if we prove a theorem for an abstract vector space, it automatically applies to arrows, matrices, functions, and signals simultaneously. This 'one-size-fits-all' logic is why linear algebra is so powerful.
section_5.example: A 'Master Key' character: A single key labeled 'Linear Algebra' that unlocks doors to Quantum Mechanics (State Vectors), Economics (Input-Output models), and AI (Neural Network weights).

outline.content: Demonstrate that polynomials or continuous functions are vectors. If you add two curves, you get a new curve. if you scale a curve, it changes height. This is the 'aha!' moment where students see vectors as more than just coordinates.

Adding two functions creates a new, combined curve.
Scaling a function changes its height or amplitude.
Like arrows, functions satisfy all eight vector axioms.
This transforms calculus into a branch of linear algebra.

outline.title: The Concept of Abstraction
outline.content: Introduce the idea that 'Vector-ness' isn't about being an arrow; it's about following a set of rules. We define a Vector Space as a collection of objects (vectors) that can be added together and scaled by numbers, while staying within the same collection.
outline.example: Think of a 'Color Mixing Robot'. If it mixes Blue and Red, it gets Purple (another color). If it uses half as much Red, it gets a lighter shade. As long as the results are still 'colors', we have the basis of a vector space.

lecture_lines: Vectors are not just arrows; they are rule followers.
A vector space is a collection of compatible objects.
Adding or scaling these objects keeps them within the set.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout(

        self.place_in_area(container, "A1", "F6")
        
        container_label = Text("Vector Space", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(container_label, "A3")
        container_label.shift(RIGHT * 0.5) # Center label roughly between A3 and A4
        
        shape1 = Triangle(color=BLUE_E).scale(0.4)

        self.place_at_grid(shape1, "B2")

        self.play(

        # We'll use shape1 and shape2 to "merge"

            run_time=1
        )
        self.add(addition_result)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate a shape being scaled (changing size) while remaining within the container in light orange (#FFDAB9).

            addition_result.animate.set_color("#FFDAB9"),
        )

            addition_result.animate.scale(1.5),

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.",
            "Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.",
            "Every space must contain a unique zero vector.",
            "Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.",
            "These rules apply to any set passing the test."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DEFAULT = "#CCCCCC"
        COLOR_COMM = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_DIST = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_VALID = "#32CD32"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axiom_names = [
            "Commutativity", "Associativity", "Additive Identity", 
            "Additive Inverse", "Distributivity (V)", "Distributivity (S)",
            "Scalar Assoc.", "Scalar Identity"
        ]
        
        axiom_mobjects = []
        # Positions: A1-A2, B1-B2, C1-C2, D1-D2
        positions = ["A1", "B1", "C1", "D1", "A2", "B2", "C2", "D2"]
        
        for i, name in enumerate(axiom_names):
            txt = Text(f"{i+1}. {name}", font_size=18, color=COLOR_DEFAULT)
            self.place_at_grid(txt, positions[i])
            axiom_mobjects.append(txt)
            self.play(Write(txt), run_time=0.3)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMM)
        )
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMM))
        
        # u + v = v + u
        u_label = MathTex("u", color=RED)
        plus1 = MathTex("+")
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=BLUE)
        eq = MathTex("=")
        v_label2 = MathTex("v", color=BLUE)
        plus2 = MathTex("+")
        u_label2 = MathTex("u", color=RED)
        
        comm_formula = VGroup(u_label, plus1, v_label, eq, v_label2, plus2, u_label2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(comm_formula, "A4", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(comm_formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Swap positions
        # Using temporary centers to avoid target drift during concurrent animation
        u1_start = u_label.get_center()
        u2_start = u_label2.get_center()
        v1_start = v_label.get_center()
        v2_start = v_label2.get_center()
        
        self.play(
            u_label.animate.move_to(u2_start),
            u_label2.animate.move_to(u1_start),
            v_label.animate.move_to(v2_start),
            v_label2.animate.move_to(v1_start),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(comm_formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Every space must contain a unique zero vector.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO)
        )
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO))
        
        # Visualizing a Zero point
        zero_point = Dot(color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(2)
        zero_label = MathTex("\\vec{0}", color=COLOR_ZERO)

        self.place_at_grid(zero_label, "D6")

section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concrete Vector
section_1.content: Briefly revisit vectors as 'arrows' in 2D or 3D space. Establish the two fundamental operations: Addition (head-to-tail) and Scalar Multiplication (stretching/shrinking). This ensures the audience understands the 'behavior' we are about to generalize.
section_1.example: An arrow pointing (3, 2) on a graph represents a force or displacement. If we double the force, the arrow stretches; if we add another force, the arrows combine geometrically.

section_2.title: The Concept of Abstraction
section_2.content: Introduce the idea that 'Vector-ness' isn't about being an arrow; it's about following a set of rules. We define a Vector Space as a collection of objects (vectors) that can be added together and scaled by numbers, while staying within the same collection.
section_2.example: Think of a 'Color Mixing Robot'. If it mixes Blue and Red, it gets Purple (another color). If it uses half as much Red, it gets a lighter shade. As long as the results are still 'colors', we have the basis of a vector space.

section_3.title: The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game
section_3.content: Present the 8 formal axioms (Commutativity, Associativity, Distributive properties, Identity, and Zero vector) through a visual checklist. Explain that any set of objects passing these tests qualifies as an 'Abstract Vector Space'.
section_3.example: Visualizing a 'Zero Element': In a space of functions, the 'Zero Vector' is the flat line y=0. In a space of matrices, it's a grid of zeros. Adding 'Zero' to any object must leave it unchanged.

section_4.title: Exotic Examples: Functions as Vectors
section_4.content: Demonstrate that polynomials or continuous functions are vectors. If you add two curves, you get a new curve. if you scale a curve, it changes height. This is the 'aha!' moment where students see vectors as more than just coordinates.
section_4.example: Imagine a 'Sound Synthesizer'. Each sound wave is a vector. Adding two waves creates a chord (superposition). Scaling a wave changes its volume. Therefore, the set of all possible sounds is an abstract vector space.

section_5.title: Why it Matters: The Power of Generalization
section_5.content: Conclude by explaining that if we prove a theorem for an abstract vector space, it automatically applies to arrows, matrices, functions, and signals simultaneously. This 'one-size-fits-all' logic is why linear algebra is so powerful.
section_5.example: A 'Master Key' character: A single key labeled 'Linear Algebra' that unlocks doors to Quantum Mechanics (State Vectors), Economics (Input-Output models), and AI (Neural Network weights).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):

        # Data from storyboard

        axes = Axes(

            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        )
        # Position axes in the center-right area
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'F6')
        self.add(axes)
        
        # Vector v (3, 2)
        v_arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            end=axes.c2p(3, 2),

            color=color_v,

        self.play(Create(v_arrow), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_w)
        )
        
        # Vector w (1, 1) starting from v's tip (head-to-tail)
        w_arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(3, 2),
            end=axes.c2p(4, 3),
            buff=0,
            color=color_w,
            stroke_width=6
        )

            buff=0,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(w_arrow), Write(w_label))
        self.play(Create(vw_res))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup addition vectors to prepare for scaling demo
        self.play(FadeOut(w_arrow), FadeOut(w_label), FadeOut(vw_res))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_scaling)
        )
        
        # Scale v by factor of 2: (6, 4)
        v_scaled_arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            end=axes.c2p(6, 4),
            buff=0,
            color=color_scaling,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        v_scaled_label = MathTex(r"2\vec{v}", color=color_scaling)

        self.play(

        lines = [
            "Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.",
            "Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.",
            "Every space must contain a unique zero vector.",
            "Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.",
            "These rules apply to any set passing the test."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DEFAULT = "#CCCCCC"
        COLOR_COMM = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FF4500"

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axiom_names = [
            "Commutativity", "Associativity", "Additive Identity", 
            "Additive Inverse", "Distributivity (V)", "Distributivity (S)",
            "Scalar Assoc.", "Scalar Identity"
        ]
        
        axiom_mobjects = []
        # Positions: A1-A2, B1-B2, C1-C2, D1-D2
        positions = ["A1", "B1", "C1", "D1", "A2", "B2", "C2", "D2"]

        self.play(
            u_label.animate.move_to(u2_start),
            u_label2.animate.move_to(u1_start),
            v_label.animate.move_to(v2_start),
            v_label2.animate.move_to(v1_start),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(comm_formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Every space must contain a unique zero vector.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO)
        )
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO))
        
        # Visualizing a Zero point
        zero_point = Dot(color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(2)
        zero_label = MathTex("\\vec{0}", color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_point, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label, "D6")
        
        self.play(Create(zero_point), Write(zero_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO)
        )
        
        # v + 0 = v
        v_label_calc = MathTex("v", color=BLUE)
        plus_zero = MathTex("+", "\\vec{0}", color=COLOR_ZERO)
        eq_v = MathTex("=", "v", color=BLUE)
        
        identity_eqn = VGroup(v_label_calc, plus_zero, eq_v).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(identity_eqn, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(identity_eqn))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(identity_eqn), FadeOut(zero_point), FadeOut(zero_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # These rules apply to any set passing the test.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_VALID)
        )
        
        # Distributive highlight
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIST))
        dist_formula = MathTex("c(u+v) = cu + cv", color=COLOR_DIST)
        self.place_in_area(dist_formula, "C4", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(dist_formula))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(dist_formula))

        # Checkmarks for all axioms
        checkmarks = VGroup()
        for axiom in axiom_mobjects:
            check = MathTex("\\checkmark", color=COLOR_VALID).scale(0.6)
            check.next_to(axiom, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            checkmarks.add(check)
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[Create(c) for c in checkmarks], lag_ratio=0.1),
            *[a.animate.set_color(COLOR_VALID) for a in axiom_mobjects]
        )
        
        final_label = Text("Valid Vector Space", color=COLOR_VALID, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_label, "E4", "F6")
        self.play(Write(final_label))
        self.play(Indicate(final_label, color=COLOR_VALID))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title_text = "Exotic Examples: Functions as Vectors"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Functions can be treated as vectors in abstract spaces.",
            "Adding two functions creates a new, combined curve.",
            "Scaling a function changes its height or amplitude.",
            "Like arrows, functions satisfy all eight vector axioms.",
            "This transforms calculus into a branch of linear algebra."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        PINK_CLR = "#FF69B4"
        CYAN_CLR = "#00FFFF"
        PURPLE_CLR = "#8A2BE2"
        HIGHLIGHT_CLR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Elements - Axes for plotting functions
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Scalar tracker for the pink wave amplitude
        amp_p = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Pink wave: f(x) = amp * sin(2x)
        # Using always_redraw to respond to amp_p changes later
        pink_wave = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda x: amp_p.get_value() * np.sin(2 * x),
            color=PINK_CLR
        ))
        
        # Cyan wave: g(x) = 0.5 * sin(3x) (static)
        cyan_wave = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x),
            color=CYAN_CLR
        )
        
        # Purple wave: h(x) = f(x) + g(x)
        # Using always_redraw to respond to amp_p changes
        purple_wave = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda x: amp_p.get_value() * np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x),
            color=PURPLE_CLR
        ))

        # Labels for the curves
        pink_label = Text("f(x)", color=PINK_CLR, font_size=20)
        cyan_label = Text("g(x)", color=CYAN_CLR, font_size=20)
        purple_label = Text("f(x) + g(x)", color=PURPLE_CLR, font_size=20)
        
        # Position labels using the grid
        self.place_at_grid(pink_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(cyan_label, "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(purple_label, "F5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Functions can be treated as vectors in abstract spaces."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(pink_wave), Create(cyan_wave))
        self.play(Write(pink_label), Write(cyan_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Adding two functions creates a new, combined curve."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE_CLR)
        )
        self.play(Create(purple_wave), Write(purple_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Scaling a function changes its height or amplitude."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PINK_CLR)
        )
        # Animate the amplitude change (scalar multiplication)
        self.play(amp_p.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Like arrows, functions satisfy all eight vector axioms."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR)
        )
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This transforms calculus into a branch of linear algebra."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Why it Matters: The Power of Generalization",
            [
                "Abstract proofs apply to arrows, functions, and matrices.",
                "One theorem can solve problems across many fields.",
                "This generalization is the core power of linear algebra."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Physics Icon (Atom)
        atom_center = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.05)
        e1 = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.3, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).rotate(PI/3)
        e2 = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.3, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).rotate(-PI/3)
        e3 = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.3, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        physics_icon = VGroup(atom_center, e1, e2, e3)
        self.place_at_grid(physics_icon, "B2", scale_factor=0.7)
        physics_label = Text("Physics", font_size=16).next_to(physics_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Economics Icon (Graph)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], x_length=0.8, y_length=0.8, 
                    axis_config={"include_ticks": False, "stroke_width": 2}).set_color(WHITE)
        # Using a fixed path for Economics graph to avoid point calculation errors
        graph_line = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_width=3)
        graph_line.set_points_as_corners([
            axes.c2p(0, 0.5, 0),
            axes.c2p(1, 1.2, 0),
            axes.c2p(2, 1.0, 0),
            axes.c2p(3, 2.5, 0)
        ])
        economics_icon = VGroup(axes, graph_line)
        self.place_at_grid(economics_icon, "C2", scale_factor=0.7)
        economics_label = Text("Economics", font_size=16).next_to(economics_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # AI Icon (Nodes)
        # Using coordinates relative to origin then moving
        n1_pos = ORIGIN
        n2_pos = RIGHT*0.6 + UP*0.4
        n3_pos = RIGHT*0.6 + DOWN*0.4
        n4_pos = RIGHT*1.2
        n1 = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, point=n1_pos)
        n2 = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, point=n2_pos)
        n3 = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, point=n3_pos)
        n4 = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, point=n4_pos)
        l1 = Line(n1_pos, n2_pos, stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)
        l2 = Line(n1_pos, n3_pos, stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)
        l3 = Line(n2_pos, n4_pos, stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)
        l4 = Line(n3_pos, n4_pos, stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)
        ai_icon = VGroup(n1, n2, n3, n4, l1, l2, l3, l4)
        self.place_at_grid(ai_icon, "D2", scale_factor=0.7)
        ai_label = Text("AI", font_size=16).next_to(ai_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Create(physics_icon), Write(physics_label),
            Create(economics_icon), Write(economics_label),
            Create(ai_icon), Write(ai_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Master Key
        key_handle = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4)
        key_shaft = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.1, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1).next_to(key_handle, RIGHT, buff=0)
        key_tooth1 = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=0.2, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1).move_to(key_shaft.get_right() + LEFT*0.1 + DOWN*0.1)
        key_tooth2 = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=0.15, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1).move_to(key_shaft.get_right() + LEFT*0.3 + DOWN*0.075)
        key_label_text = Text("Linear Algebra", font_size=14, color="#FFD700").next_to(key_shaft, UP, buff=0.1)
        master_key = VGroup(key_handle, key_shaft, key_tooth1, key_tooth2, key_label_text)
        
        self.place_in_area(master_key, "C4", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(master_key, shift=LEFT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Key rotation to simulate unlocking
        self.play(Rotate(master_key, angle=30*DEGREES, about_point=key_handle.get_center(), rate_func=wiggle))
        
        # Success state: Icons turn green
        self.play(
            physics_icon.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            physics_label.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            economics_icon.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            economics_label.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            ai_icon.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            ai_label.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

outline.title: The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game
outline.content: Present the 8 formal axioms (Commutativity, Associativity, Distributive properties, Identity, and Zero vector) through a visual checklist. Explain that any set of objects passing these tests qualifies as an 'Abstract Vector Space'.
outline.example: Visualizing a 'Zero Element': In a space of functions, the 'Zero Vector' is the flat line y=0. In a space of matrices, it's a grid of zeros. Adding 'Zero' to any object must leave it unchanged.

storyboard.title: The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game
lecture_lines: Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.
Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.
Every space must contain a unique zero vector.
Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.
These rules apply to any set passing the test.
animations: Show a list of 8 axiom names appearing one by one in light gray (#CCCCCC).
Highlight 'Commutativity' (#FFD700) and show u + v = v + u swapping positions visually.
Highlight 'Zero Vector' (#FF4500) and show a vector v added to a zero point, resulting in v unchanged.
Highlight 'Distributive' (#1E90FF) and show c(u+v) = cu + cv expanding with color-coded variables.
Apply a checkmark to all items and label the space 'Valid Vector Space' in bright green (#32CD32).

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.",
            "Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.",
            "Every space must contain a unique zero vector.",
            "Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.",
            "These rules apply to any set passing the test."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DEFAULT = "#CCCCCC"
        COLOR_COMM = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_DIST = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_VALID = "#32CD32"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axiom_names = [
            "Commutativity", "Associativity", "Additive Identity", 
            "Additive Inverse", "Distributivity (V)", "Distributivity (S)",
            "Scalar Assoc.", "Scalar Identity"
        ]
        
        axiom_mobjects = []
        # Positions: A1-A2, B1-B2, C1-C2, D1-D2
        positions = ["A1", "B1", "C1", "D1", "A2", "B2", "C2", "D2"]
        
        for i, name in enumerate(axiom_names):
            txt = Text(f"{i+1}. {name}", font_size=18, color=COLOR_DEFAULT)
            self.place_at_grid(txt, positions[i])
            axiom_mobjects.append(txt)
            self.play(Write(txt), run_time=0.3)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMM)
        )
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMM))
        
        # u + v = v + u
        u_label = MathTex("u", color=RED)
        plus1 = MathTex("+")
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=BLUE)
        eq = MathTex("=")
        v_label2 = MathTex("v", color=BLUE)
        plus2 = MathTex("+")
        u_label2 = MathTex("u", color=RED)
        
        comm_formula = VGroup(u_label, plus1, v_label, eq, v_label2, plus2, u_label2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(comm_formula, "A4", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(comm_formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Swap positions
        # Using temporary centers to avoid target drift during concurrent animation
        u1_start = u_label.get_center()
        u2_start = u_label2.get_center()
        v1_start = v_label.get_center()
        v2_start = v_label2.get_center()
        
        self.play(
            u_label.animate.move_to(u2_start),
            u_label2.animate.move_to(u1_start),
            v_label.animate.move_to(v2_start),
            v_label2.animate.move_to(v1_start),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(comm_formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Every space must contain a unique zero vector.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO)
        )
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO))
        
        # Visualizing a Zero point
        zero_point = Dot(color=COLOR_ZERO).scale(2)
        zero_label = MathTex("\\vec{0}", color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_point, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label, "D6")
        
        self.play(Create(zero_point), Write(zero_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO)
        )
        
        # v + 0 = v
        v_label_calc = MathTex("v", color=BLUE)
        plus_zero = MathTex("+", "\\vec{0}", color=COLOR_ZERO)
        eq_v = MathTex("=", "v", color=BLUE)
        
        identity_eqn = VGroup(v_label_calc, plus_zero, eq_v).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(identity_eqn, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(identity_eqn))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(identity_eqn), FadeOut(zero_point), FadeOut(zero_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # These rules apply to any set passing the test.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_VALID)
        )
        
        # Distributive highlight
        self.play(axiom_mobjects[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIST))
        dist_formula = MathTex("c(u+v) = cu + cv", color=COLOR_DIST)
        self.place_in_area(dist_formula, "C4", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(dist_formula))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(dist_formula))

        # Checkmarks for all axioms
        checkmarks = VGroup()
        for axiom in axiom_mobjects:
            check = MathTex("\\checkmark", color=COLOR_VALID).scale(0.6)
            check.next_to(axiom, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            checkmarks.add(check)
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[Create(c) for c in checkmarks], lag_ratio=0.1),
            *[a.animate.set_color(COLOR_VALID) for a in axiom_mobjects]
        )
        
        final_label = Text("Valid Vector Space", color=COLOR_VALID, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_label, "E4", "F6")
        self.play(Write(final_label))
        self.play(Indicate(final_label, color=COLOR_VALID))
        self.wait(2)

        amp_p = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Pink wave: f(x) = amp * sin(2x)
        # Using always_redraw to respond to amp_p changes later
        pink_wave = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(

        ))

            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x),
            color=CYAN_CLR
        )
        
        # Purple wave: h(x) = f(x) + g(x)
        # Using always_redraw to respond to amp_p changes
        purple_wave = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda x: amp_p.get_value() * np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x),
            color=PURPLE_CLR
        ))

        pink_label = Text("f(x)", color=PINK_CLR, font_size=20)
        cyan_label = Text("g(x)", color=CYAN_CLR, font_size=20)

        # Position labels using the grid
        self.place_at_grid(pink_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(cyan_label, "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(purple_label, "F5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Functions can be treated as vectors in abstract spaces."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(pink_wave), Create(cyan_wave))
        self.play(Write(pink_label), Write(cyan_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Concept of Abstraction
outline.content: Introduce the idea that 'Vector-ness' isn't about being an arrow; it's about following a set of rules. We define a Vector Space as a collection of objects (vectors) that can be added together and scaled by numbers, while staying within the same collection.
outline.example: Think of a 'Color Mixing Robot'. If it mixes Blue and Red, it gets Purple (another color). If it uses half as much Red, it gets a lighter shade. As long as the results are still 'colors', we have the basis of a vector space.

            "Scalar Assoc.", "Scalar Identity"
        ]
        
        axiom_mobjects = []
        # Positions: A1-A2, B1-B2, C1-C2, D1-D2, A2... wait.
        # Let's use A1, B1, C1, D1 for first 4 and A2, B2, C2, D2 for next 4.
        positions = ["A1", "B1", "C1", "D1", "A2", "B2", "C2", "D2"]
        
        for i, name in enumerate(axiom_names):
            txt = Text(f"{i+1}. {name}", font_size=18, color=COLOR_DEFAULT)

            axiom_mobjects.append(txt)

        )

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title_text = "Exotic Examples: Functions as Vectors"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Functions can be treated as vectors in abstract spaces.",
            "Adding two functions creates a new, combined curve.",
            "Scaling a function changes its height or amplitude.",
            "Like arrows, functions satisfy all eight vector axioms.",
            "This transforms calculus into a branch of linear algebra."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        PINK_CLR = "#FF69B4"
        CYAN_CLR = "#00FFFF"
        PURPLE_CLR = "#8A2BE2"
        HIGHLIGHT_CLR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sine.svg]
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wave.svg]
        sine_icon_pink = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sine.svg", color=PINK_CLR)
        sine_icon_cyan = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sine.svg", color=CYAN_CLR)
        wave_icon_purple = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wave.svg", color=PURPLE_CLR)
        
        # Elements - Axes for plotting functions
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Scalar tracker for the pink wave amplitude
        amp_p = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Pink wave: f(x) = amp * sin(2x)
        # Using always_redraw for amplitude animation
        pink_wave = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda x: amp_p.get_value() * np.sin(2 * x),
            color=PINK_CLR
        ))
        
        # Cyan wave: g(x) = 0.5 * sin(3x) (static)
        cyan_wave = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x),
            color=CYAN_CLR
        )
        
        # Purple wave: h(x) = f(x) + g(x)
        # Using always_redraw to reflect changes in pink_wave amplitude
        purple_wave = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda x: amp_p.get_value() * np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x),
            color=PURPLE_CLR
        ))

        # Labels for the curves
        pink_label = Text("f(x)", color=PINK_CLR, font_size=20)
        cyan_label = Text("g(x)", color=CYAN_CLR, font_size=20)
        purple_label = Text("f(x) + g(x)", color=PURPLE_CLR, font_size=20)
        
        # Positioning labels and icons according to VideoCritic feedback
        # Issue 27: Move f(x) label to row B for margin
        self.place_at_grid(pink_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(sine_icon_pink, "B4", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # Issue 28: Move g(x) label to B6 for balance
        self.place_at_grid(cyan_label, "B6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(sine_icon_cyan, "A6", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # Issue 26: Use area for long purple label to avoid overlap
        self.place_in_area(purple_label, "F5", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_icon_purple, "F4", scale_factor=0.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Functions can be treated as vectors in abstract spaces."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(
            Create(pink_wave), 
            FadeIn(sine_icon_pink), 
            Write(pink_label),
            Create(cyan_wave),
            FadeIn(sine_icon_cyan),
            Write(cyan_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Adding two functions creates a new, combined curve."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE_CLR)
        )
        self.play(
            Create(purple_wave), 
            FadeIn(wave_icon_purple), 
            Write(purple_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Scaling a function changes its height or amplitude."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PINK_CLR)
        )
        # Animate the amplitude change (scalar multiplication)
        self.play(amp_p.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Like arrows, functions satisfy all eight vector axioms."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR)
        )
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This transforms calculus into a branch of linear algebra."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_CLR)
        )
        self.wait(3)
